reproduction_target: Method-development paper introducing scDRP (sparsity-regularized beta-VAE disentangled representation + soft-conditional optimal transport in latent space) for individual treatment effect (ITE) estimation from single-cell perturbation data. Reproduction target = the full computational pipeline: simulation of synthetic single-cell perturbation data, scDRP model training, conditional-OT / barycentric-projection ITE and CATE estimation, baseline comparisons against CINEMA-OT and scGen (both via pertpy), BCPlaid biclustering of the ITE matrix (R biclust) with a two-stage bicluster-merging procedure, clusterProfiler GO enrichment of the resulting functional gene modules, Gaussian-process latent interpolation for unseen dosages, ITE vector composition for combined treatments, and the evaluation metrics (RMSE / PCC on top-3000 HVGs, MMD on top-200 HVGs with RBF kernel + median heuristic) plus UMAP visualization. All analysis is on previously published public datasets (Kang, Hagai, Dong, Adamson, sciplex4); there is no wet-lab component. Note the paper sits close to the tool-methods route (its primary contribution is the scDRP Python package), but every reported result is a computational step, so it is routed pure-computational.
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool/analysis-invocation from Methods sections 4.1-4.7 plus the Results text naming the baselines. scDRP is split into three steps (simulation, model training, conditional-OT/ITE estimation) because they are separately parameterized in the prose; the two baselines are separate steps because each is a distinct named method invoked through pertpy; bicluster merging is separate from BCPlaid because its thresholds (OS > 0.03, IoU > 0.3) are stated independently. UMAP visualization is folded into the evaluation step. No paper-specific analysis scripts, notebooks, driver code, or per-dataset configuration files are cited anywhere; the code-availability statement points only at the scDRP package repository.

steps.label: Simulation of synthetic single-cell perturbation datasets (Methods 4.6): latent components from a Gaussian mixture, cell-type labels from Dirichlet(K), rank-preserving shift of z_d, non-linear neural map to mean expression with selective latent masks, ZINB sampling with BCV-linked dispersion and dropout, N/2 control + N/2 treatment cells; 20 replicates per setting

scDRP model training (Methods 4.1): sparsity-regularized beta-VAE with encoders q(z_d|x,a,w) and q(z_u|x,w), HSCIC conditional-independence loss, hard-concrete gate variable m for latent-dimension selection, MSE (half-Gaussian) or ZINB reconstruction loss

Conditional optimal transport in the disentangled latent space + barycentric projection -> counterfactual samples, ITE and CATE/CATU (Methods 4.2); squared-Euclidean distance and transport cost, alpha (conditional strength) and beta (transport-cost weight), two projection strategies (full latent vs z_d only)
Baseline comparison: CINEMA-OT (COT), 'implemented with Python library pertpy'
Baseline comparison: scGen, 'implemented with Python library pertpy'

Biclustering of the estimated ITE matrix with the BCPlaid algorithm, 'available via R package biclust, with the default parameters' (Methods 4.3); biclustering performed per condition (cell type / perturbation)

Bicluster summarization and two-stage merging into functional gene modules (Methods 4.3): removal of genes broadly present across biclusters within a condition, within-condition merging by overlap score OS > 0.03, cross-condition merging by IoU > 0.3, then cell assignment to FGMs
GO / functional enrichment analysis of differential FGMs with R package clusterProfiler (Methods 4.3)

Unseen-dose response prediction via latent-space interpolation (Methods 4.4): dose concatenated with one-hot perturbation index, Gaussian-process regression conditioned on w with hyperparameters optimized by maximizing log marginal likelihood, standardized-residual transplantation, decoding through the pre-trained VAE decoder

Synthetic effect estimation for multiple treatments via ITE vector composition (Methods 4.5): correlation r_AB between tau_A and tau_B interpreted as cosine, parallelogram law / cosine theorem to infer absolute combined effect; validated on PBMC single vs combined stimulations (IFNb+TNFa, IFNb+IFNg, IFNb+IL-6)

Evaluation and visualization (Methods 4.7): RMSE of ITE/CATE on simulated data; RMSE and PCC of mean expression on top-3000 HVGs on real data; MMD on top-200 HVGs with Gaussian/RBF kernel estimated by V-statistic, bandwidth by median heuristic; UMAP visualization of observed vs counterfactual cells and of ITE matrices

headline.static_readiness: 0/11 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: 7/11 (64%) computational steps reach RI at the stage-1 ceiling; 4/11 cap at NI. The RI-eligible steps are the ones served by the public scDRP package (simulation, model training, conditional-OT/ITE estimation, bicluster merging, GP dose interpolation, ITE vector composition, evaluation metrics), whose dependency versions are exactly pinned in the repository requirements.txt. The four NI steps are the third-party invocations described only by name - CINEMA-OT and scGen 'implemented with pertpy' (no version, no parameters), BCPlaid via R biclust (default parameters stated but no R/biclust version), and clusterProfiler enrichment (no version, no ontology/cutoff/background). Even a favourable stage-2 code read cannot lift these four without version and parameter information that does not exist in either the paper or the repository. The dominant global blocker is the absence of any paper-specific driver code: the repository ships the scDRP package plus one R biclustering example, but no per-figure analysis scripts, no per-dataset hyperparameter configuration, and no random seeds, so exact numeric reproduction of the reported figures is not demonstrable from the prose.
headline.coverage: 11 computational steps assessed from Methods 4.1-4.7 plus the Results baseline description. W = 0 (no wet-lab component; all datasets are previously published and re-used). Both a data-availability and a code-availability statement are present and both resolve.

gaps.missing: The code-availability statement points only at the scDRP package repository (https://github.com/sjl-sjtu/scDRP). The repository landing page lists LICENSE, README.md, biclustering_example.R, docs, requirements.txt, setup.py, src - i.e. the library plus one R example. There are no per-figure or per-dataset analysis scripts/notebooks, no simulation driver, no baseline-comparison harness, and no configuration files reproducing the reported benchmarks and case studies.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit an analysis repository (or an analysis/ directory in the same repo) containing the simulation driver, per-dataset training configs, the CINEMA-OT / scGen comparison harness, the biclustering + merging + enrichment pipeline, and the figure-generation notebooks, keyed to figure numbers.

gaps.where: Software environment for the whole pipeline
gaps.missing: No conda environment file, no lockfile, no container image or digest, and no version numbers in the paper prose at all. The repository requirements.txt does carry exact '==' pins (matplotlib==3.10.7, numpy==2.3.4, pandas==2.3.3, POT==0.9.5, scanpy==1.11.5, scikit_learn==1.7.2, scipy==1.16.3, torch==2.3.1+cu121, umap_learn==0.5.7), but this is an unresolved requirements list, not an environment closure: no transitive-dependency resolution, no python version, no CUDA/driver constraint beyond the +cu121 wheel tag, and no R-side environment at all (R, biclust, clusterProfiler, and its annotation databases are entirely unpinned). pertpy - the library carrying both baselines - is not in requirements.txt and is unversioned everywhere.
gaps.how_to_close: Ship a conda-lock / pixi.lock / uv.lock or a container digest covering both the Python and R sides, including pertpy and the clusterProfiler annotation database snapshot, and state the Python and R versions.

gaps.where: C1 simulation; C2 scDRP training; C3 conditional OT; C9 GP interpolation
gaps.missing: No random seeds are reported anywhere for the stochastic components: simulation sampling (GMM, Dirichlet, ZINB), VAE weight initialization and minibatch shuffling, the hard-concrete gate sampling, the train/validation split (README example shows valid_prop=0.1 with early stopping), and UMAP initialization. The paper reports mean +/- 1.96SE over 20 simulation replicates but does not state how replicates are seeded.
gaps.how_to_close: Record and publish the seeds (or a seed list per replicate) for simulation, model training, and embedding, and state the determinism settings used for torch/CUDA.

gaps.where: C2 scDRP training and C3 conditional OT - per-dataset hyperparameters
gaps.missing: The paper describes the hyperparameters qualitatively only ('a relatively small value of alpha can be used' when cell types are known, 'a larger value of alpha is required' otherwise) and reports sensitivity analyses (Fig. 2b, 2d) without stating the values actually used for each reported result. Latent dimensions, hidden-layer sizes, beta, sparsity/l0 coefficients, HSCIC weight, epochs, batch size, and learning rate appear only in the README's illustrative example (latent_dependent=50, latent_independent=50, hidden_layers=[512,512], beta=2, sparse_coef=0, l0_latent=0.001, lambda_hsic=0.2, epoch_num=200, batch_size=64, lr=1e-3) which is a generic snippet, not the per-dataset settings behind the figures. The reconstruction-likelihood choice (half-Gaussian/MSE vs ZINB) per dataset is not stated.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish a per-dataset configuration table (or config files) giving latent dimensions, beta, sparsity and HSCIC weights, likelihood choice, optimizer/lr/epochs, and the alpha/beta/projection-strategy/OT-solver settings used for every reported figure.

gaps.where: C4 CINEMA-OT; C5 scGen; C8 clusterProfiler
gaps.missing: The two baselines are described only as 'implemented with Python library pertpy' with no parameters, no preprocessing description, and no version. clusterProfiler enrichment is named with no ontology, no organism annotation database, no p-value/q-value cutoffs, no multiple-testing method, and no background gene universe.
gaps.how_to_close: State the baseline invocation parameters (or ship the calling code), the pertpy version, and for enrichment give the ontology, OrgDb and its version, cutoffs, adjustment method, and background universe.

gaps.where: C11 evaluation; preprocessing across all real-data steps
gaps.missing: Preprocessing is not described as a reproducible step: how raw counts were normalized/log-transformed per dataset, how the top-3000 and top-200 HVGs were selected (which flavor, computed on which cell subset, before or after splitting control/treatment), how cells were filtered, and how control/treatment groups were defined per dataset are not stated. Dataset-specific subsetting (e.g. which cell types and perturbations enter each figure) is only implied by the Results text.
gaps.how_to_close: Document the per-dataset preprocessing recipe (or ship it as code): filtering thresholds, normalization, HVG selection flavor and n_top_genes, and the exact control/treatment group definitions and cell-type subsets.

gaps.where: Dataset resolution - Kang, Hagai, Dong, Adamson, sciplex4
gaps.missing: All five datasets are public and reachable, but they are cited at the level of a distributing resource rather than a versioned artifact: Kang and Hagai 'available via pertpy package' (pertpy's dataset loaders fetch from a remote store whose contents can change and which is not version-pinned here), Adamson and sciplex4 via the scPerturb Zenodo record 13350497 (a versioned record - good), and Dong via DRYAD doi:10.5061/dryad.4xgxd25g1 (versioned - good). The PBMC combined-stimulation dataset used for the vector-composition validation is cited only as reference [4]. No file-level identifiers or checksums are given for any dataset.
gaps.how_to_close: Give the exact file names / accession-level identifiers (and checksums) for each dataset used, and pin the pertpy version whose loaders were used for Kang and Hagai.

gaps.missing: The GitHub repository sjl-sjtu/scDRP has zero releases and zero tags, and the paper cites no commit SHA. The default branch has moved since posting (repository pushed_at 2026-06-14, preprint posted 2025-11-24), so the code state corresponding to the reported results is not identifiable. There is also no Zenodo/Software Heritage archive of the code.
gaps.how_to_close: Tag a release corresponding to the manuscript, archive it (Zenodo DOI or Software Heritage), and cite that identifier in the code-availability statement instead of the bare repository URL.
